stories.title: ILTACON Europe Wrap-Up - ILTA
stories.ltme_summary: ILTA publishes a wrap-up of ILTACON Europe, its legal technology conference. The extract is only a summary line, so the sessions, speakers and outcomes covered are not visible here.
stories.hook: ILTA publishes its wrap-up of ILTACON Europe

stories.title: SRA has its wings clipped again, this time over access to LPP material: where next for its investigatory powers?
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal reports on Carter-Ruck & Amersi v SRA [2026] EWHC 2416, in which the High Court held that the SRA cannot access material subject to legal professional privilege for its investigations. The SRA has obtained a leapfrog certificate and will seek permission to appeal to the Supreme Court.
stories.hook: High Court rules SRA cannot access privileged material, and the regulator will seek a Supreme Court appeal

stories.title: Legal AI in 2027: From adoption to accountability
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal publishes a trends piece on legal AI for 2027, arguing that firms must govern AI agents at scale. It covers agent identity and permissions, the risk of inherited access to confidential material, and activity logs. The piece frames cost control and proof of commercial value as the next priorities.
stories.hook: Solicitors Journal says 2027 will turn on managing AI agent identities and permissions

stories.title: Law Society warns AML reforms could weaken consumer protection
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal reports that the Law Society of Scotland has warned MPs that moving AML supervision of Scottish solicitors to the FCA could weaken consumer protection and raise costs. It cites a conveyancing gap and concerns about devolved legislation. The Financial Services and Markets Bill is at committee stage.
stories.hook: Law Society of Scotland tells MPs FCA takeover of AML supervision would weaken consumer protection

stories.title: Freeths advises on Toolstation sale
10th Circuit Adopts Certification Rule for AI-Assisted Filings, Becomes First US Appeals Court to Do So
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor reports that the 10th Circuit has adopted a certification rule for AI-assisted filings, making it the first US appeals court to do so. The rule lets the court deem an affected issue waived or strike a noncompliant document, alongside existing sanctions for attorneys who fail to comply with its AI mandate.
stories.hook: 10th Circuit becomes first US appeals court with an AI certification rule for filings

stories.title: Clients Are Turning to AI Before Their Lawyers, Posing Risks to Firms
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Tech Monitor, relaying a piece from another outlet, says more clients are consulting chatbots for legal guidance before speaking to lawyers. It argues lawyers must set expectations about AI answers and protect privilege more deliberately. The item is a short summary with no data.
stories.hook: Clients turning to chatbots before lawyers creates privilege and expectation risks for firms

stories.title: An Interview With David Pogue: AI Will Change A Lot. We’ll Cope
From Faster to Fundamentally Different: 5 Key Takeaways from TLTF Summit 2026
The Nightly Waterfall
15 Organizations Call On Congress To Address Abuse Of Drug Patent System
OpenAI Held Talks With AI Native Law Firm
stories.hook: OpenAI reportedly tried to recruit staff from an AI-native law firm, which turned the offer down

stories.title: Catherine Bamford Joins Document Drafter as Evangelist
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer reports that Copenhagen-based Document Drafter has hired Catherine Bamford as an evangelist to support firms moving to decentralised AI document automation. Co-founder Michael Bjerg Hansen says the platform offers agentic templating and MCP support. Bamford describes the move as part of a shift in how templates are built.
stories.hook: Document Drafter hires Catherine Bamford as evangelist for decentralised AI document automation

stories.title: A More Measured Approach to AI Fluency
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer publishes a sponsored piece arguing that AI enablement teams need better ways to measure how well lawyers use GenAI, not just whether they log in. It cites TITANS research commissioned by Harvey, which sets out a five-level AI Fluency Framework, and describes richer product data on prompts and built assets.
stories.hook: Harvey-commissioned research proposes a five-level AI fluency framework for law firms

stories.title: Building Legora’s Canadian legal AI presence from the ground up
stories.ltme_summary: Canadian Lawyer profiles Legora's Canadian build-out, with Daniel Himmel describing the company's growth from a team of about 50 to over 1,000 and its first Canadian customer in December 2025. It names firmwide deployments at McMillan, Fasken and Stewart McKelvey and says the Walter AI acquisition completed in March 2026.
stories.hook: Legora says it moved from its first Canadian customer to firmwide deployments in under a year

stories.title: Daniel Himmel on building legal AI at Legora in Canada
stories.ltme_summary: Canadian Lawyer publishes a podcast episode in which Tim Wilbur interviews Daniel Himmel, who runs Legora's Canadian operation. They discuss his career from articling to Legora and how legal AI platforms sit on foundation models. The page lists other Canadian legal technology coverage.
stories.hook: Legora's Canadian lead says the hardest part of legal AI adoption is not the technology

stories.title: Legal Tech Developer Fired Over Site Errors Wins Claim
stories.ltme_summary: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech carries a headline only, saying a legal technology developer fired over site errors has won a claim. The extract gives no company name, court, amount or date, so the employment case cannot be assessed from this item.
stories.hook: Legal tech developer dismissed over site errors wins employment claim, Law360 reports

stories.title: Reversa Raises €750K After Joining A&O Shearman Program
Startup Alley Gets A Shake-Up for 2027, As Applications Open for ABA TECHSHOW’s Annual Pitch Competition
stories.ltme_summary: LawSites reports that applications are open for the 11th annual Startup Alley at ABA TECHSHOW, with a deadline of 3 January 2027. The 2027 format cuts finalists to eight, moves to a bracket, drops public voting for finalists and allows consumer-facing products. TECHSHOW takes place on 3 March 2027 in Chicago.
stories.hook: ABA TECHSHOW Startup Alley drops public voting and admits consumer legal products for 2027

stories.title: Clifford Chance matches Milbank scale for US associates as Pallas ups bonus stakes
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Clifford Chance has matched the US associate pay scale set by Milbank in June, becoming the second magic circle firm to do so. Base pay runs from $235,000 for the class of 2026 to $455,000 for the class of 2019 and above. The story also links to Pallas bonus moves.
stories.hook: Clifford Chance matches Milbank's US associate pay scale, from $235,000 to $455,000

stories.title: Aiello on call as Cravath and Freshfields lead on Sanofi’s $41bn Insmed acquisition
Weil exits continue as Paul Weiss, Davis Polk and Jones Day hire partners across the US
‘There’s stability in scale’ – why Cahill’s star finance team chose Latham
Solicitor struck off after sending client screenshot of fake email
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that Kimberley Clift, formerly of Lawrence Stephens, has been struck off after sending a client a screenshot of a fabricated email. She had wrongly told the client a stamp duty refund of about £6,500 was in progress. The tribunal approved the agreed outcome with the SRA and ordered £4,000 in costs.
stories.hook: Lawrence Stephens solicitor struck off over fabricated email about stamp duty refund

stories.title: SRA compliance, hybrid working, and IT: What your managing partner needs to know
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures publishes a piece sponsored by AspiraCloud on SRA compliance and hybrid working. It says 33 per cent of UK law firms in the provider's early sector survey were unsure whether their IT arrangements would meet SRA expectations if questioned. The article sets out a checklist covering MFA, access controls, AI tools and supervision.
stories.hook: A third of UK law firms are unsure their IT would satisfy the SRA, AspiraCloud says

stories.title: Does the AI Growth Lab mark a turning point for responsible AI in legal services?
stories.hook: OneAdvanced argues the AI Growth Lab could help legal AI earn trust under UK regulators

stories.title: Fladgate selects Laurel for automated timekeeping
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that Fladgate has selected Laurel to automate timekeeping. The extract available is only the site's verification message, so no details of the scope, timing or contract are visible.
stories.hook: Fladgate picks Laurel for automated timekeeping

stories.title: Catherine Bamford joins Document Drafter as chief evangelist
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that Catherine Bamford has joined Document Drafter as chief evangelist. The extract is only a verification message, so her remit and start date are not visible here.
stories.hook: Catherine Bamford joins Document Drafter as chief evangelist

stories.title: Agentic AI regulatory startup Reversa raises €750k in pre-seed funding
stories.ltme_summary: Legal IT Insider reports that Reversa, a startup focused on regulation of agentic AI, has raised €750k in pre-seed funding. The extract available is only a verification message, so the investors and the company's product details are not visible.
stories.hook: Agentic AI regulatory startup Reversa raises €750k pre-seed

stories.title: Hogan Lovells Cadwalader raises US associate pay as London gap widens
Six months in, AI-native Norm Law is closing in on the US top 200
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that Norm Law, an AI-native New York firm, says it is on course to reach Am Law 200 revenue levels within a year, six months after full launch. The firm has 65 lawyers and 29 partners, and is powered by Norm Ai, which has raised over $260m. It describes outcome-based and subscription pricing.
stories.hook: Norm Law says it is on track for Am Law 200 revenue within a year of its April launch

stories.title: Linklaters hires Weil’s European antitrust head in major coup
Ex-Goodwin lawyers raise $11m for fund formation startup
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that Intelligent Legal Solutions, a London fund formation startup founded by former Goodwin lawyers, has raised $11m in Series A funding co-led by Aquiline and BlackFin. The company says it counts nine of the ten largest US fund formation firms as customers and plans its first US offices.
stories.hook: Intelligent Legal Solutions raises $11m Series A and plans first US offices

stories.title: Startup offers reviews of clients' AI-generated documents
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Conclusive Legal, an SRA-authorised platform founded by former Linklaters litigation case manager Jessica Fitzgerald, offers solicitor review of client-drafted documents. Fixed fees start at £295, with court and pre-action reviews from £595. The platform targets SME disputes up to £100,000.
stories.hook: Conclusive Legal offers solicitor review of clients' AI-drafted documents from £295

stories.title: Housing legal aid expansion 'financially unfeasible' for providers
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Law Society says the Legal Aid Agency's plan to extend housing and debt legal aid in eight regions does not address inadequate funding and is financially unfeasible for firms. The LAA wants providers to sign up by 4 December. Property tribunal cases rose 56 per cent year on year in April to June.
stories.hook: Law Society says extra housing legal aid contracts will not fix underfunding
entities: Law Society of England and Wales

stories.title: Only 14% of victims aware of Victims' Code rights
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that a survey for the Victims' Commissioner of more than 6,000 victims found 80 per cent had not heard of the Victims' Code. Only 14 per cent knew their rights. Crown Court cases open for a year or more reached a record 23,706 in September.
stories.hook: Survey finds 80 per cent of victims have not heard of the Victims' Code

stories.title: Solicitor who faked email to keep client at bay struck off
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal has struck off Kimberley Clift, a solicitor who created a fake email to keep a client waiting over a stamp duty refund. The tribunal ordered £4,000 in costs. Clift admitted dishonesty and agreed the outcome with the SRA.
stories.hook: Solicitor struck off after faking an email to a client over a stamp duty refund

The People Who Got You Home For Thanksgiving
‘The Best Justice System In The World’ Has A Jury Problem
How LexisNexis Protégé Helps Attorneys Meet Emerging AI Standards
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law carries a LexisNexis piece on how its Lexis+ with Protégé product can help attorneys meet emerging AI expectations. It cites New York guidance dated 26 October 2026 that names LexisNexis as a verification source, and California's SB 574, signed 30 September 2026 and effective 1 January 2027. The article describes Shepard's Verify, which checks citations and will soon check quotations, and says customer data is not used to train LexisNexis AI models.
stories.hook: LexisNexis positions Protégé and Shepard's Verify as tools for meeting New York and California AI duties for attorneys

stories.title: Which insurance defence boutiques stand above the rest?
Feds’ new Divorce Act study aims to improve family violence response
BC names Geoff Cowper, Fasken partner, as deputy attorney general
stories.ltme_summary: Canadian Lawyer reports that Geoffrey Cowper, a Vancouver partner at Fasken who led the firm's litigation group for over a decade, has been appointed deputy attorney general of British Columbia from 20 November. Fasken's managing partner Clarke Barnes praised him in a firm release. The article draws on Fasken and government releases.
stories.hook: Fasken litigation partner Geoff Cowper appointed BC deputy attorney general

In A First, 10th Circuit Addresses AI With New Rules

Ohio Lawyer Suspended Amid Fake AI Cites, Unpaid $647K
stories.ltme_summary: Law360 Pulse Legal Tech carries a one-line summary that an Ohio lawyer has been suspended after filing fake AI citations and failing to pay a $647K judgment. The extract is only the headline and summary line, so the disciplinary order, the court and the dates are not visible here.
stories.hook: Ohio lawyer suspended over fake AI citations and an unpaid $647K debt

stories.title: Linklaters’ AI Lawyer Named by Forbes in AI Law List
stories.ltme_summary: LawFuel carries a Linklaters announcement that Forbes has named partner Ieuan Jolly, chair of the firm's US technology, media and telecoms and IP practice, as one of America's Top AI Lawyers. Linklaters says the honour follows earlier recognition from the Financial Times and Chambers USA. The release is the firm's own account and gives no date beyond the article's publication.
stories.hook: Linklaters says Forbes has named Ieuan Jolly one of America's Top AI Lawyers

stories.title: Property Law’s New Competitive Threat Isn’t AI. It’s the Firm Down the Road
stories.ltme_summary: LawFuel reports on a Digital Conveyancing Summit panel hosted by Search Acumen, where live polling found 43 per cent of around 500 property lawyers named rival firms adopting AI faster as their biggest threat. Search Acumen's Andrew Lloyd argued that data, not AI, is the core problem. A JLL executive said fewer than 40 per cent of organisations starting AI pilots had formal training or governance. The article draws on a Search Acumen release.
stories.hook: 43 per cent of property lawyers at a Search Acumen panel cite rivals' faster AI adoption as top threat

stories.title: How A Focused Injury Practice Serves Clients In Small Communities
Why Cravath Still Holds the Purse Strings in BigLaw’s Salary Race
Financial Account Transfers: What the Law Requires Companies to Disclose
Small firms, big opportunities: how legal AI is levelling the playing field
stories.ltme_summary: Craig Matthews, UK chief executive of LEAP Legal Software, writes on Legal Futures that legal AI can narrow the gap between small and large firms. He argues that smaller practices can adopt tools faster and that AI can take on routine tasks such as reviewing leases and drafting client correspondence. The piece is a sponsored opinion and sets out no adoption figures.
stories.hook: LEAP's Craig Matthews argues legal AI can level the playing field for small firms

stories.title: Big tech firms using their lawyers for “performative compliance”
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that Inside Track's UK Big Tech Group, a group of more than 20 senior professionals from UK arms of large technology firms, has published a memo called Where is the Law? The memo says legal teams are asked whether they are likely to face repercussions rather than whether conduct is lawful, and that new staff are asked to sign lifelong NDAs. The findings are based on insiders' accounts.
stories.hook: Inside Track's Big Tech Group says tech firms spend on lawyers for 'performative compliance'

stories.title: Minister drops major hint on allowing electronic wills
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that justice minister Sarah Sackman has given the strongest signal yet that the government will modernise wills, including electronic wills. She responded to a House of Lords committee letter on the Law Commission's Modernising wills report, which made 31 recommendations. Sackman said a formal response would be published as soon as possible.
stories.hook: Justice minister Sarah Sackman signals electronic wills reform after Law Commission report
entities: House of Lords justice and home affairs committee

stories.title: Form: Apply to vary or discharge a domestic abuse protection order made in a family court: Form DA3
stories.hook: HMCTS updates form DA3 as domestic abuse protection orders go national in England and Wales

stories.title: Form: Apply for a domestic abuse protection order in a family court: Form DA1
stories.ltme_summary: HM Courts and Tribunals Service has updated form DA1, the application for a domestic abuse protection order in a family court. The page records a change dated 25 November 2026 reflecting that the orders can now be applied for across England and Wales. The form includes a supporting witness statement template and guidance on the applicant's personal connection to the respondent.
stories.hook: HMCTS form DA1 now reflects England and Wales-wide domestic abuse protection orders

stories.title: Form: Apply for a non-molestation or occupation order: Form FL401
stories.ltme_summary: HMCTS has updated its guidance page for the FL401 application for a non-molestation or occupation order. The page now points applicants who need protection from domestic abuse to a domestic abuse protection order instead, where eligible. The update is dated 25 November 2026 and the form itself is unchanged in the extract.
stories.hook: HMCTS FL401 guidance now points eligible applicants to domestic abuse protection orders

stories.title: Apply for a domestic abuse protection order in a county court
stories.ltme_summary: HMCTS has updated its guidance on applying for a domestic abuse protection order in a county court, where the applicant has an ongoing civil case with the respondent. The guidance sets out the forms to use, the rules on serving applications and orders, and that there are no court fees. The page is dated 25 November 2026 and reflects the national extension of the orders.
stories.hook: HMCTS county court guidance for domestic abuse protection orders updated for national rollout

stories.title: Form: Ask for permission to apply for a domestic abuse protection order on behalf of someone else: Form DA2
stories.ltme_summary: HMCTS has updated form DA2, which asks a family court for permission to apply for a domestic abuse protection order on behalf of another person. The page is dated 25 November 2026 and records that the orders can now be applied for across England and Wales. The form sets out that the process differs where an ongoing county court civil case exists.
stories.hook: HMCTS form DA2 updated for third-party applications for domestic abuse protection orders

stories.title: Apply for a domestic abuse protection order in a family court
stories.ltme_summary: HMCTS has updated its guidance on applying for a domestic abuse protection order in a family court. The guidance explains who can apply, the respondent's personal connection requirement, the witness statement wording, and service rules. It notes that county court cases must use the county court route instead. The page is dated 25 November 2026.
stories.hook: HMCTS family court guidance on domestic abuse protection orders updated for England and Wales

stories.title: Procedure rules and forms for civil proceedings in magistrates’ courts and the Crown Court
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice publishes residual civil procedure rules and appeal forms for magistrates' and Crown Courts

stories.title: What to do if you receive a domestic abuse protection notice or order
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice has published a guide for people who receive a domestic abuse protection notice or an order. It says the orders are available across England and Wales from November 2026 and that breaching an order can be a criminal offence. The guide explains that police must apply to the magistrates' court within 48 hours of issuing a notice.
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice guide sets out duties under domestic abuse protection notices from November 2026

stories.title: Guidance: Domestic abuse protection notices and orders: guidance for local authorities and support services
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice issues guidance for councils and support services on protection orders

stories.title: Domestic abuse protection notices and orders: guidance for victims of domestic abuse
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice has published a guide for victims on domestic abuse protection notices and orders. It explains that the orders are available across England and Wales from November 2026, that applications can be made by police, relatives or social workers, and that a court can make an order on its own initiative. The page is dated 25 November 2026.
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice victims' guide explains who can seek domestic abuse protection orders

stories.title: Guidance: Domestic abuse protection notices and orders: guidance for legal practitioners
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice has published guidance for legal practitioners and advice agencies on domestic abuse protection notice and order cases, focusing on family and county court proceedings. The guidance is available as a PDF and in Welsh. The page is dated 25 November 2026 and the extract gives no further detail of its contents.
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice guidance for lawyers on domestic abuse protection order cases in family and county courts

stories.title: New AI Export Controls: Implications for AI Companie...
stories.ltme_summary: Dechert, a law firm, has published a client note on new US AI export controls and what they mean for AI companies. The extract is only the article opening, so the scope of the controls is not confirmed here.

stories.title: Changes to the HIPAA Privacy Rule: What OCR’s Final Rule Means for Covered Entities and Business Associates | Publications | Kirkland & Ellis LLP
stories.ltme_summary: Kirkland & Ellis summarises HHS OCR's final rule modernising the HIPAA Privacy Rule, published on 19 November 2026. The rule cuts the access response window from 30 to 15 calendar days, limits fees for inspection, and allows access through personal health apps. Compliance becomes mandatory in July 2027.
stories.hook: Kirkland & Ellis maps HHS OCR's HIPAA final rule: 15-day access deadline from July 2027

stories.title: Elite Shortlisted for Cloud Transformation of the Year in the 2026/27 Cloud Award
stories.hook: Elite shortlisted for Cloud Transformation award, citing 44 per cent rise in cloud adoption

stories.title: The Tenth Circuit Adopted Certification Rule for Human Review of Filings: Artificial Intelligence Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin, writing on eDiscovery Today, reports that the Tenth Circuit has adopted Rule 46.5(B)(4), requiring lawyers to certify that a human has verified citations and quotations in briefs, including AI-assisted ones. The rule also allows the court to deem issues waived or strike filings. It takes effect on 1 January 2027 with the 2027 Tenth Circuit Rules. The post relays a National Law Journal report.
stories.hook: Tenth Circuit adopts human-verification certification rule for AI-assisted filings from 1 January 2027

stories.title: MCP in eDiscovery: What it is and How it Works: eDiscovery Best Practices
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin's eDiscovery Today explains the Model Context Protocol and how Lexbe applies it through Lexbe Connect for Claude. The post says the AI works within the user's existing permissions and that the platform controls which tools are exposed. Lexbe sponsors the site and promotes a webinar on 9 December 2026.
stories.hook: Lexbe explains how MCP lets AI assistants work inside eDiscovery platforms

stories.title: Neutral ESI Expert Ordered After Parties Fail to Comply with July Order: eDiscovery Case Law
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin reports on Lighthouse Healthcare Center v National Fire & Marine Insurance, a Central District of California order of 20 October 2026. Magistrate Judge Anna Park partly granted sanctions, ordered a third-party neutral ESI expert, and required a revised privilege log. She said AI is a tool and not a substitute for compliance with a court order.
stories.hook: Court orders neutral ESI expert after parties' AI-assisted review ignored July discovery order

stories.title: HHS Finalizes HIPAA Privacy Rule Amendments: What to Do Before the July 19, 2027, Compliance Deadline
stories.ltme_summary: Troutman Pepper Locke says HHS has finalised amendments to the HIPAA Privacy Rule, with a compliance deadline of 19 July 2027. The firm's note sets out what covered entities should do before that date.

stories.title: Meta’s $25-Billion Verdict Lessons: Data Governance and Privacy Operations
stories.ltme_summary: Troutman Pepper Locke has published a commentary on lessons from a reported $25bn verdict against Meta, focusing on data governance and privacy operations. The piece is a law firm view rather than a news report of the ruling.

How Much Autonomy Should Litigators Give AI Agents?
stories.ltme_summary: Everlaw reports on a panel at Everlaw Summit '26 on how litigators should delegate work to agentic AI. Speakers included Alexander Nocks of Perry Law, Steve Shuldman of Harvey and Everlaw's Pauline Day. They argue teams should decide which work is safe to delegate and keep human review for privilege and strategy decisions.
stories.hook: Everlaw summit panel says litigators should delegate only low-risk work to agentic AI

stories.title: [Recording] Simulive: Who’s Really Applying? How to Stop Hiring Fraud Before Day One
stories.ltme_summary: Mitratech is promoting a recorded simulive session on hiring fraud, including AI-generated documents, deepfakes and synthetic identities. The session is listed for 9 December and the recording is now available.

stories.title: What $71.9M in Outside Counsel Invoices Reveals About Billing Guideline Compliance
stories.ltme_summary: Onit says a review of $71.9m of outside counsel invoices by its Spend Agent tool found 18 per cent, worth $12.9m, did not match billing guidelines. The release cites its own research showing 92 per cent invoice-level accuracy for the tool against 72 per cent for experienced lawyers. It also describes Sentry, Auto and Off modes.
stories.hook: Onit says Spend Agent flagged $12.9m of $71.9m in outside counsel invoices as off-guideline

stories.title: Introducing Spellbook's Docusign Integration
stories.ltme_summary: Spellbook has launched an integration with Docusign. Users can select contracts in a deal workspace, send Docusign envelopes to counterparties, and have signed copies sync back and store in the repository. Spellbook's intake agent also picks up signed copies that arrive by email.
stories.hook: Spellbook launches Docusign integration to send and file signed contracts in its repository
